findings.title: The process type check skips killing spawned workers
findings.body: Workers are created using multiprocessing.get_context("spawn").Process, which produces SpawnProcess instances. These inherit from BaseProcess, not multiprocessing.Process, so this isinstance check is false for production workers. When a worker is declared hung, it is therefore left running while a replacement is started for the same shards. This leaks workers and allows the old worker to resume flushing concurrently with its replacement. Check against multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess or explicitly distinguish threads from processes before killing the worker.

findings.title: Do not skip remaining workers when the join deadline expires
findings.body: Once the shared deadline expires, this break bypasses cleanup for every remaining worker. This happens if next_step.join consumes the timeout or an earlier flusher uses the remaining time. Setting stopped does not interrupt a worker blocked on Redis or a Kafka future, so those workers can survive a rebalance and continue operating on shards assigned to new workers. Apply the deadline only to graceful waiting, and still terminate all surviving processes before returning.
